newsitem.title: ITALY: INA takes one pct of San Paolo.
newsitem.headline: INA takes one pct of San Paolo.

text.p: Italian insurance group INA said on Tuesday it agreed to buy a one percent stake in Italy's largest bank, San Paolo di Torino, as part of the Turin-based bank's privatisation programme.
An INA statement after a group board meeting said the investment bank would hold the shares for a "period of stabilisation" of at least six months.
Investment bank IMI said earlier it too would buy a stake of around one percent for the same the stabilisation period.
IMI also said it empowered its executive committee to pursue negotiations that could lead to IMI becoming a core shareholder of San Paolo.

Currently, a foundation indirectly holds 65 percent of San Paolo, but this is planned to be reduced to 25 percent by offering shares to the public and a group of core shareholders. IMI currently holds a two percent stake in San Paolo and has an option, which expires in June to raise its stake to five percent.
